findings.issue: Every require message raised after the first external call of a function (186 of them) is printed as a raw memory revert, its text only visible as hex words or not at all (the _validateReceiver ones), while the same messages before any call print as revert with 'invalid _amount' (stakeGmx 740-741). The calls between them also lose their function and arguments (617 P2 lines), e.g. the second call of each _validateReceiver pair shows no _receiver argument.
findings.rule: Decode the Error(string) layout relative to any base b: mem[b] = 0x08c379a0 << 224, mem[b + 4] = 32, mem[b + 36] = n, n bytes at b + 68, then revert(b, 68 + ceil32(n)) is 'revert with <string>', whatever b is. With the c00600 bound (mem[64] >= 96, stores at mem[64] + k never alias slot 64), 'x - mem[64]' with x = mem[64] folds to 0, so the revert range starts at b.

findings.issue: A loop whose first statement is its exit test is printed as while True; a phi of two identical expressions is not merged, so the return-size check reads _10 - 128; gmxAmount > 0 recomputes the sum instead of _61 > 0 and _validateAmount's check is kept under it (P11).
findings.rule: 'while True: if c: exit; body' is 'while not c: body' then exit; a phi whose operands are equal is that operand; reuse a named value instead of its expression, and drop a check implied by the dominating condition.

notes: Long functions reviewed by structure (calls, branches, reverts, storage writes, events, loops): signalTransfer, batchRestakeForAccounts, unstakeGmx, unstakeEsGmx, compound, handleRewards, handleRewardsV2, batchCompoundForAccounts, acceptTransfer (900-2900 lines each, made of the inlined _compound/_restakeForAccount/_stakeBnGmx/_syncVotingPower call sequences). Call order, targets (stor7 stakedGmxTracker ... stor16 externalHandler), argument order, the nonReentrant/onlyGov order, the 'transfer not signalled' mapping check and delete, the inStrictTransferMode allowance check, sendValue and the voting-power mint/burn branches all match the source. Removed checks are exact (extcodesize before a second static call to the same address; _validateAmount under 'if amount'). Source loops: batchStakeGmxForAccounts (1046), batchRestakeForAccounts (1671), batchCompoundForAccounts (9489), multicall (539), all readable whiles; their bodies suffer P2 and raw reverts. Implicit loops: 6 address[] and 2 bytes[] calldata decoders are fine; P7 = 32 copy loops of the 16 inlined safeTransferFrom (call data copy + error-message copy), multicall's 2 bytes copies, makeExternalCalls' bytes copy and 3 address[] re-encoding loops (mem[u] = Bytes(12, 0), mem[t + 12 len 20]); P3 = the zero-init of new bytes[](n) (532). P8: call buffers printed beside decoded calls (614-618 and every stake call of stakeGmx/stakeEsGmx/unstake*), 80 dead 'SafeMath: subtraction overflow' string allocations (= 30 / string word), withdrawToken 422-431 (incl. mem[176 len 16] = uint128(_addr >> 32)), sha3 scratch mem[0]/mem[32]. P11: 'assert s < mem[128]' in the batch loops, the kept _validateAmount check. P15: slot 18 (inStrictTransferMode, govToken, votingPowerType, inRestakingMode) is 'stor18 is uint256' and setVotingPowerType writes 'stor18 = _param1 << 168 | stor18 >> 176 << 176 | uint168(stor18)' while setGovToken uses address(stor18.field_8). Events are shown by topic hash (names unknown to the database), and 19 log data lists are raw memory (counted in P2).
summary: Semantically faithful (every call, branch, revert and write of the source is present and in order), but after the first external call of a function the free-memory pointer is lost: 617 call lines lose their function and arguments and 186 revert reasons are hidden in raw memory, which makes the long reward functions very hard to read.
